verdict.rationale_short: NVDA's Q1 beat ($81.6B revenue vs $79.2B estimate; Q2 guide $91.0B) confirms the AI capex narrative and resolves the morning's primary binary risk. WTI fell ~5% to ~$98 on Middle East peace talks, partially relieving the inflationary pressure that drove the morning selloff. However, the 30Y remains above the 5.0% regime trigger (~5.09%), FOMC April minutes confirmed an 8-4 hawkish vote with CME pricing 63% year-end hike odds, and NVDA's AH reaction (initially -2% sell-the-news, recovered to +1.93%) introduces Thursday open uncertainty. The HOLD is maintained; BUY upgrade requires NVDA $226+ at Thursday's open + SPX reclaiming 7,460 + 30Y below 5.15% for 30 minutes.

bear_case: FOMC April minutes were the most hawkish since October 1992, and equity markets ignored them because NVDA's numbers were better — that ordering has historically reversed sharply when the macro input catches up to the fundamental one. If the 30Y spikes back above 5.20% Thursday morning on hawkish Fed speaker commentary, the NVDA-driven rally fails to hold and SPX rolls back below 7,400. The SpaceX IPO ($75B raise, June 12 trading) represents the largest equity capital drain in history arriving in three weeks; institutional managers funding the SPCX allocation will begin raising cash from winning positions — which now include the AI complex. If SPX closes below 7,400 with the 30Y above 5.20% on Thursday, the HOLD-to-BUY upgrade path is invalidated; reinstate Step Aside.
